author: blu
body: The occurrence analyser: the highest-leverage pre-pass in the GHC simplifier architecture. For a definition it answers, per binder in that definition, how many times the binder is referenced within its scope -- Dead (0), Once, or Many (two or more). That single fact is what a GHC-style simplifier (WS-D3, not this unit) consumes to make two rewrites free and safe: drop dead let-bindings -- DCE stops being a pass -- and inline an occurs-once binding unconditionally, because inlining a value used exactly once neither duplicates work nor grows code.

author: blu
body: An IrDoBind scopes over the statements AFTER it, not the whole block: a bind's classification is read from the free map of the rest of the sequence, and the name is removed from that map before it rises past the bind. The do-notation the 2.22 lowering fix made real is a sequence in which each bind scopes over the tail.

author: blu
body: A map from free name to its count, and the walk's result: the free map of a subtree together with the classifications collected for every binder seen inside it. The binder list threads through the walk as an accumulator so its order is the traversal order -- a subtree's binders before the binder that scopes them -- and is deterministic.

author: blu
body: A branch's pattern binds over its guard and body only. Guard and body are analysed, their maps unioned, and each pattern variable classified and stripped; the surviving map joins the scrutinee's above.

author: blu
body: A rendering of the analysis for a whole chapter, one line per definition as `OCC defname: name=Class, name=Class`. The `occ-report` pass in Passes.codex returns these lines through the same out-of-band violation channel `ir-check` uses, so `-Passes occ-report` dumps the analysis of every definition to the compile log without rewriting a single node.
